solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Cher’s duo rarely sang together (8)

indicatorNotes.rarely: done rarely means done in an unusual way, so the letters take an unusual order

blocks.note: the letters of CHERS and DUO rearranged

annotation.surface: A note that Sonny and Cher seldom actually sang as a pair.
annotation.walkthrough: Cher's duo was Sonny & Cher, which pulls you toward the pop act, but the words are only letters to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: To chorus is to sing or speak together, so chorused means sang together.

entries.clue: Use a PC (6)

blocks.note: cop means worth or use, as in 'not much cop'
a, as in 'ten pounds a head', means per

annotation.surface: An instruction to go and work at a computer.
annotation.walkthrough: PC looks like a personal computer; here it is a police constable. COP as 'use' survives mainly in the phrase 'not much cop', meaning no good.
annotation.definitionFit: A PC is a police constable, and copper is British slang for a police officer.

entries.clue: Prophet filling in for a clergyman (6)

indicatorNotes.filling in: the answer is the filling inside the words that follow

blocks.note: fOR A CLErgyman

annotation.surface: A visiting prophet taking the service while the vicar is away.
annotation.walkthrough: 'filling in' reads as standing in for someone, but it points to the letters sitting inside 'for a clergyman'.
annotation.definitionFit: An oracle is one who delivers prophecies, so a prophet.

entries.clue: Secret service technique (9)

blocks.note: secret in the sly, deceitful sense
a way of serving in tennis or volleyball with the arm swung below the shoulder

annotation.surface: A spy manual describing how the secret service works.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Secret service' runs together as the spies; split it after 'Secret' and the service becomes a serve in a ball game.
annotation.definitionFit: Underhand means done secretly and deceitfully, and it also names a serve made with the arm swung below the shoulder.

entries.clue: Retract arms after each pitch (3,4,5)

blocks.note: EA is the standard abbreviation for each
the pitch of a sound is its tone
swords are arms, weapons

annotation.surface: An army ordered to pull back its weapons after every sales pitch.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue gives arms first but 'after' puts them last, behind each and pitch.
annotation.definitionFit: To eat one's words is to take back what one said, to retract it.

entries.clue: Article points to right solution (6)

blocks.note: AN is the indefinite article
the compass points South, West and East
R is the abbreviation for right

annotation.surface: A newspaper article that steers the reader toward the right solution.
annotation.walkthrough: 'points to' reads as indicates, but 'points' are three compass points and 'to' only joins them to 'right'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the word for whatever resolves a question or problem.

entries.clue: Relations that turned up without agreement (5)

indicatorNotes.turned up: in a down answer, turning a word up means writing it bottom to top
indicatorNotes.without: without in its old sense of outside, so NOY goes round OK

blocks.note: yon is an old word for that, as in 'yon hill'; turned up, it reads NOY
OK signals agreement

annotation.surface: Family members who showed up without having agreed to come.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Relations' looks like relatives, but it is the sexual kind. 'without' means outside here, not lacking.
annotation.definitionFit: Nooky is a slang word for sexual relations.

entries.clue: One jumps a wall or scrambles over (8)

indicatorNotes.scrambles: to scramble is to jumble, so the letters of A WALL OR are mixed

blocks.note: the letters of A WALL OR rearranged
O is the scoring abbreviation for an over in cricket

annotation.surface: An athlete who either leaps a wall or clambers across it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'scrambles over' looks like one climbing phrase; 'over' is split off as the cricket O. A wallaroo is a large Australian kangaroo.
annotation.definitionFit: A wallaroo is a kind of kangaroo, an animal that moves by jumping.

entries.clue: Colourful dress: evidence a star is going away (3,5)

annotation.definition: evidence a star is going away

blocks.note: red is a colour
a shift is a simple straight dress

annotation.surface: A bright gown, and a celebrity walking out of the limelight.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'star' leaving looks like a celebrity departing; it is a real star moving away from Earth.
annotation.definitionFit: Light from a star receding from us is stretched toward the red end of the spectrum, the red shift.

entries.clue: Praise leads to promotion and less reviews (8)

indicatorNotes.leads: the leads of words are their first letters

blocks.note: first letters of Promotion and Less
audits are formal reviews

annotation.surface: An employee whose praise brings a promotion and fewer performance reviews.
annotation.walkthrough: 'leads to' reads as causes; 'leads' takes the first letters and only 'promotion' and 'less' supply them.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the plural: applause and acclaim, many voices of praise.

entries.clue: Front light out (6)

blocks.note: the bow is the front of a ship
an LED is a light-emitting diode, a small light

annotation.surface: The headlamp on the front has gone out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'light out' looks like a bulb failing, but 'out' is a cricket dismissal, where a batter is bowled when the ball hits the stumps.
annotation.definitionFit: In cricket a batter who is bowled is out.

entries.clue: See Edward with another chap’s sweets (7,5)

blocks.note: to spot is to see
Ted is short for Edward
Dick is another man's name, so Dick's

annotation.surface: An invitation to watch Edward sharing a friend's sweets.
annotation.walkthrough: In British usage a sweet is also a dessert; spotted dick is a steamed suet pudding studded with currants.
annotation.definitionFit: Spotted dick is a British pudding, and puddings are called sweets.

entries.clue: Mathematician’s rule about conserving energy (5)

indicatorNotes.about: turned about, so the letters of RULE are rearranged
indicatorNotes.conserving: the rearranged RULE keeps E safe inside it

blocks.note: the letters of RULE rearranged
E is the physics symbol for energy

annotation.surface: A physicist's law about the conservation of energy.
annotation.walkthrough: The conservation of energy is real physics, which makes 'rule about' read as a law; 'about' mixes RULE and 'conserving' holds the E. Leonhard Euler was an 18th-century Swiss mathematician.
annotation.definitionFit: Named by example: Leonhard Euler, the 18th-century Swiss who founded graph theory.

entries.clue: Strong ale not considered for minor ailment (5,4)

blocks.note: nappy is an old word for heady, foaming ale
a rash act is one not thought through

annotation.surface: Drinking strong ale without a thought, as a cure for something trivial.
annotation.walkthrough: A nappy is the British word for a diaper, so nappy rash is diaper rash.
annotation.definitionFit: Nappy rash is a common, minor skin irritation in babies.

entries.clue: Make a loud noise build up, perhaps (5,3,4)

blocks.note: a crowd that raises the roof is very loud
literally, a builder lifting a roof higher

annotation.surface: Noisy building work going on above you.
annotation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' flags that the second meaning is an example: extending a house upward is one way to raise its roof.
annotation.definitionFit: To raise the roof is to make a great noise, cheering or shouting.

entries.clue: Parent worried on river transport (9)

indicatorNotes.worried: worried, as a dog worries a bone, so PARENT is shaken into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of PARENT rearranged
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

annotation.surface: An anxious parent fretting about a child travelling by boat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'transport' looks like travel on the river, but it is the verb meaning to delight.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: to transport someone is to carry them away with delight, which is what enrapturing does.

entries.clue: Scruffy lie-abeds let themselves down (8)

indicatorNotes.Scruffy: scruffy means untidy, so the letters are in a mess

blocks.note: the letters of LIE-ABEDS rearranged

annotation.surface: Slovenly late risers who have disappointed everyone.
annotation.walkthrough: 'let themselves down' reads as failed; taken literally it is lowering yourself down a rope.
annotation.definitionFit: To abseil is to lower yourself down a rock face on a rope.

entries.clue: Trifles cook holds ready, keeping soft (8)

indicatorNotes.holds: a cook who holds something has it inside, so FRY wraps round the rest
indicatorNotes.keeping: to keep something is to hold on to it, so RIPE closes round the P

blocks.note: to fry is to cook
ripe fruit is ready to eat
P is piano, soft in music

annotation.surface: A cook with some fancy desserts ready and kept soft.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Trifles' suggests the pudding a cook might hold, but it means trivial things. The containers nest: soft goes inside ready first, and that goes inside cook.
annotation.definitionFit: Frippery is showy trivial stuff, trifles.

entries.clue: Uninterested in babe sporting pierced lugholes (5,2,5)

indicatorNotes.sporting: the pierced lugholes sport the babe: TOT sits between BORED and EARS

blocks.note: a hole bored is pierced
a tot is a small child
lughole is British slang for ear

annotation.surface: A bored child wearing earrings in newly pierced ears.
annotation.walkthrough: TOT goes between the two words for 'pierced lugholes'.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: so weary of something that it could make you cry, the far end of uninterested.

entries.clue: Sign chopped by a battle-axe (6)

indicatorNotes.chopped by: VIRGO is cut apart and A goes into the gap

blocks.note: Virgo is a sign of the zodiac
the A as written

annotation.surface: A zodiac sign hacked apart by an axe.
annotation.walkthrough: 'battle-axe' looks like the weapon doing the chopping, but it is the definition: a fierce woman.
annotation.definitionFit: A battle-axe and a virago are both an aggressive, domineering woman.

entries.clue: Key added to a map on purpose (6)

blocks.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side
an end is an aim or purpose

annotation.surface: Someone adding a key to a map deliberately.
annotation.walkthrough: 'on purpose' reads as deliberately, but it splits: 'on' is the cricket leg side and 'purpose' is END.
annotation.definitionFit: A specialist sense: the panel explaining the symbols on a map or chart is called by this name.

entries.clue: After the first, the other hit often described (9)

indicatorNotes.After the first: what is left after the first letter has gone

blocks.note: 'a bit of the other' is a British euphemism for sex
SEX without its first letter
to pound is to hit repeatedly

annotation.surface: Once past the first opponent, the other was hit again and again.
annotation.walkthrough: 'the first' and 'the other' look like a pair of things; 'the other' is a coy British euphemism for sex, and 'After the first' removes its S.
annotation.definitionFit: To expound is to set out and explain in detail, to describe.

entries.clue: University philosopher’s employment (5)

blocks.note: U is the abbreviation for university
a sage is a wise philosopher

annotation.surface: A philosopher's job at a university.
annotation.walkthrough: 'employment' looks like a job, but it means use.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: employment here means the act of using something, not a job.

entries.clue: Best two or three maybe (5)

blocks.note: best in quality, top grade
2 and 3 are numbers divisible only by themselves and one

annotation.surface: Picking the top two or three from a list.
annotation.walkthrough: 'maybe' says two and three are examples of a prime.
annotation.definitionFit: Prime means of the best quality, and a prime is a number divisible only by itself and one.

entries.clue: Short song heard from Spooner’s room (6)

indicatorNotes.heard from Spooner’s: Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so swap the first sounds of WEE LAY

blocks.note: wee is small, a lay is a song; swap W and L

annotation.surface: A brief tune drifting out of the Reverend Spooner's study.
annotation.walkthrough: Wee is Scottish and British for small; lay is an old word for a song or ballad.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: room to manoeuvre, a margin of freedom; the word began as a ship's sideways drift downwind.

entries.clue: Right Charlie brought in by a junior minister (8)

indicatorNotes.brought in by: C is brought inside A CURATE

blocks.note: the A as written
Charlie is C in the NATO alphabet
a curate is an assistant to a parish priest

annotation.surface: An idiot recruited by a junior government minister.
annotation.walkthrough: A 'junior minister' sounds like government, but it is a minister of religion, the curate. 'Right Charlie' is British for a complete fool.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a figure that is right is correct, free of error.

entries.clue: A poet that’s boring to study (6)

blocks.note: a dry subject is dull
a den is a private study

annotation.surface: A poet whose work is tedious to study.
annotation.walkthrough: 'study' reads as a verb, but it is the room. John Dryden was a 17th-century English poet.
annotation.definitionFit: John Dryden was England's first Poet Laureate.

entries.clue: Member of a rock band circulating a drug (8)

annotation.definition: Member of a rock band circulating

blocks.note: the A as written
an anabolic drug of the kind bodybuilders misuse

annotation.surface: A rock musician passing drugs around.
annotation.walkthrough: The rock band is the asteroid belt, a band of rocks orbiting the Sun, and 'circulating' is its orbit.
annotation.definitionFit: An asteroid is one of the rocks orbiting in the asteroid belt.
